solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 8 across to 6); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Editor wants introduction to electrics in oven guide

indicators.note: in places the editor and the opening letter inside the other word

parts.note: a baker works an oven, so the person is defined by the oven here

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter, so only the start of electrics is used

explanation.surface: An editor wants to add a chapter on electrical wiring to a cookery guide for ovens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oven' is a cryptic stretch for BAKER, one who uses an oven. Baedeker guides were the famous German travel handbooks.
explanation.definitionFit: Baedeker was a publisher of travel handbooks, so the name became a byword for any guidebook.

clue.text: Local dignitary, man hiding in tree

indicators.note: the man goes into hiding, so those letters vanish from the longer word

parts.note: an alderman is a senior member of a local council

explanation.surface: A town councillor has climbed a tree to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a common waterside tree of the birch family.

clue.text: Bet all hours, morning and afternoon?

definitions.meaning: a wager on the winners of two named races in one day's racing
read literally: something done every day, and done twice over, morning and afternoon

explanation.surface: Someone gambles round the clock, morning and afternoon alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily double is a racing bet on two races; the phrase also describes something happening twice each day.

clue.text: Shout of fright goes up, getting sweetheart to faint?

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: eek is the comic-strip squeal of fright
a lover is a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A scream of fright as a sweetheart goes weak at the knees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes up' turns EEK into KEE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To keel over is to collapse or pass out, a colloquial way to say swoon.

clue.text: Some adoration that's animated in bishop — one seeking a signal from above

definitions.text: one seeking a signal from above

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters between the bishop's two letters

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the style of a bishop

indicators.note: animated means stirred into lively motion, so the letters are set moving into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bishop shows lively adoration, as if receiving a sign from heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' looks like a quantifier but is anagram fodder too; RR (Right Reverend) is a crossword convention for a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers of this kind study the radio waves that reach Earth from space, a playful take on heavenly signals.

clue.text: Agreement's not quiet — I have to give voice

indicators.note: not tells us the quiet letter is absent from the agreement

parts.note: a pact is an agreement
P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: An accord that is far from quiet lets someone speak out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'voice' is the grammatical term, not a speaking voice.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the active is the voice in which the subject performs the verb, as opposed to the passive.

clue.text: Modern design in zone, not a place to find amusement?

indicators.note: in places the design letters within the shortened zone
not drops one letter a from the zone word

parts.note: an area is a zone
CAD, computer-aided design, is a modern way of designing

explanation.surface: Somebody puzzles over whether a modernist building zone counts as somewhere fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: an amusement arcade is full of slot machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement arcades are halls of slot machines and video games, so this is one example of the word's sense.

clue.text: Duck not wanting lake leaves

indicators.note: not wanting means doing without, so the lake letter is dropped

parts.note: the teal is a small duck
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A duck that dislikes the lake flies off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a verb but is the noun: dried leaves for brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink is brewed from the dried leaves of the Camellia plant, so the leaves themselves carry the name.

clue.text: Church official and archdeacon circling street with representation of Mary

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the title surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Ven, the Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

indicators.note: a representation is a new rendering, so the name's letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A churchman and an archdeacon walk round a street carrying a statue of the Virgin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation of' rearranges the name to RYMA; an archdeacon is styled the Venerable.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestryman is a member of a parish vestry, the committee running church business.

clue.text: Notice the deputy offering guidance

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper
vice is a prefix meaning deputy, used here as a noun for the deputy

explanation.surface: A notice says the second-in-command is giving out tips.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel or recommendation given to someone is the same thing as guidance.

clue.text: Girl involved in fraud losing it, down the social ladder

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so the girl goes into the shortened fraud word
losing means the word it drops out of the fraud word

parts.note: deceit is fraud or trickery
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl caught up in a scam loses her standing in society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is not a pronoun here but the two letters removed, leaving DECE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has fallen in status, lost their class, is described with this borrowed French word.

clue.text: Host of unsound mind, not the first

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is missing

parts.note: barmy is British slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A party giver is a little crazy, though not the first one to be so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' means a great multitude, not someone throwing a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is an old word for a great number, especially a body of soldiers, as in the heavenly host.

clue.text: Instrument, one emitting note in a bedroom disturbingly

indicators.note: in places the shortened word within the rearranged letters
something disturbed is thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: emitting means sending out, so the letter is given off from the word one

parts.note: taken as written before losing a letter
n. is the abbreviation for note, as in a footnote reference

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is played very loudly in someone's bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbingly' rearranges A BEDROOM to OBDAMORE; n. for note is the footnote abbreviation, a rarer device.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe d'amore is a mezzo-soprano member of the oboe family, much used by Bach.

clue.text: Maiden with bad heel may be used in advertising campaign

definitions.text: may be used in advertising campaign

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
ailing means poorly, unwell
to heel over is to lean, the same as a ship's list

explanation.surface: A young woman with a sore heel is roped into a promotional drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heel' is the nautical verb for leaning, not the back of a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A roster of addresses for sending promotional material is a standard tool of direct marketing.

clue.text: Son with boozy types drinking round — they may sink quite low

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the drinkers swallow the round letter

parts.note: topers are heavy drinkers
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A son and his drinking pals are sinking another round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink quite low' sounds moral but means bending down.
explanation.definitionFit: People who bend their bodies forward and down do literally sink low.

clue.text: Jewish scholar stimulated afresh after losing energy

indicators.note: afresh means anew, so the remaining letters are made into something new
after losing tells us the energy letter is gone before the shuffle

parts.note: taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A Jewish scholar feels newly inspired after running out of steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after losing energy' removes an E from STIMULATED; 'afresh' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar devoted to the Talmud, the body of rabbinic law and commentary.

clue.text: Foot with first sign of infection attended by a doctor

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A foot showing early infection is seen by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' is a metrical foot in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody a foot of one short syllable then one long is this, the basic unit of much English verse.

clue.text: Half of crackers fail to go off? Ridiculous!

indicators.note: to go off is to explode, so the letters are blown apart and reformed
half of a word is its first half here, the opening four letters

explanation.surface: Christmas crackers that fail to bang: how absurd!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes CRAC from CRACKERS; 'go off' scrambles CRAC and FAIL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absurd enough to belong in a farce is ridiculous.

clue.text: One that could be an ace driver?

definitions.text: One that could be an ace driver?

parts.words: One that could be an ace driver?
parts.note: reads as a skilled motorist, but a card of one suit can be an ace and a golfer's driver is one of these too

explanation.surface: Who might turn out to be a brilliant motorist?
explanation.walkthrough: The ace is a playing card and the driver a golf stick; the word covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: Clubs is a card suit with its own ace, and in golf the driver is the longest-hitting stick in the bag.

clue.text: Groups again sing badly after authentic start

indicators.note: after says the shuffled letters come after the authentic word, which forms the start

parts.note: real means authentic, genuine

indicators.note: done badly, the letters of the word are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: A choir regroups after singing poorly at the start of a real performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns SING into IGNS.
explanation.definitionFit: To align again is to bring back into line, in other words to arrange or group anew.

clue.text: Celebrity dispatching article in English — a variant of it

indicators.note: dispatching means getting rid of, so the article is sent away

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A star drops an article written in English, a version of the language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the definition points back to English, so the answer is a variety of English.
explanation.definitionFit: Strine is the jocular name for broad Australian speech, from Australian said in that accent.

clue.text: Note what may be ideal companion to great gin?

definitions.meaning: in music, the second degree of a major or minor scale

definitions.text: what may be ideal companion to great gin?
definitions.meaning: read as two words: a super mixer, the perfect partner for a fine gin

explanation.surface: A tasting note on which mixer best suits a premium gin.
explanation.definitionFit: The supertonic is the scale degree just above the tonic, and a splendid mixer for gin would be a super tonic.

clue.text: Number of spectators in evening at Edinburgh

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Counting the crowd at an evening event in Scotland's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The attendance figure at a sports match, as recorded through the turnstiles, is called this.

clue.text: Old character dithering outside hospital

indicators.note: outside means the indecisive word wraps round the hospital letter

parts.note: someone torn between choices is dithering
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: An elderly eccentric hovers indecisively outside the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old character' is a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorn was a runic letter used in Old English for the th sound, so it is an archaic character.

clue.text: Note thanks miners for guarding one metallic element

parts.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
ta is informal British for thanks

indicators.note: guarding means keeping safe inside, so the union surrounds the one

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A thank-you note to miners for protecting someone in a metal works.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUM is Britain's National Union of Mineworkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Titanium is a strong, light metal, number 22 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Commander in long story that sees leader deposed

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here removed from office

parts.note: a saga is a long story

explanation.surface: A commander features in an epic tale in which the chief is overthrown.
explanation.definitionFit: An aga is a military commander or chief officer in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Impertinent girl has on tunic

parts.note: a chit is a cheeky or impudent young woman

explanation.surface: A cheeky young woman is wearing a tunic.
explanation.definitionFit: The chiton was the long woollen or linen garment worn by men and women in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Gas in eastern district of Kent in short supply

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the district loses its last letter

parts.note: Thanet is a district at the north-east tip of Kent

explanation.surface: Gas is running low in an eastern part of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; Thanet is its north-eastern corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethane is a colourless hydrocarbon gas found in natural gas.

clue.text: Telling boy to embrace minority school subject

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the name wraps round the subject

parts.note: Reg is a boy's name, short for Reginald
Latin is a subject taken by relatively few pupils

explanation.surface: A boy is being told to take up a little-studied subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrating or recounting a story is another way of saying telling it.
